phrases.latin: In scālīs mōbilibus cum Theodōrus, «Mitte mē, tata!» clāmitāns, manū patris dīmissā sōlus stāre vellet
phrases.english: When Theo, on the escalator, kept shouting “Let me go, Dad!” and wanted to let go of his hand and stand by himself

sources: Lewis & Short: mitto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 99, 102, 322.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
